answer: Pair each epoch's paid work as a single-winner contest over one fixed job, assigned blind to several identities at once. A sybil operator gains nothing by adding clones: they bid against themselves for the same pot, duplicating effort while total payout stays flat, like prospectors crowding one onyx vein in the tundra instead of finding new ground. Honest solo agents face real rivals, so quality rises; a farm's tenth clone only cannibalizes its other nine and leaves its jade uncut.
